questions.question: Economic geography studies how
choices: political borders change without regard to people
economic activities are distributed across places and connected to geographic conditions
weather operates without affecting human activity

questions.question: A factory locates near a port to reduce shipping time for imported materials. Which location factor is most important?

A region grows wheat efficiently while another produces electronics efficiently. Specialization can support trade because each region may
choices: focus on activities where it has a comparative advantage
produce every good at the same cost

questions.question: Why have many manufacturers located some production near ports or major transport corridors?
choices: Ports eliminate the need for workers
Those locations can reduce the cost and time of moving inputs and finished products

questions.question: A mining region sells raw minerals abroad but imports many finished products. Which economic pattern may this illustrate?
choices: Complete control of all stages of production
Unequal positions in a global production chain

questions.question: Which indicator can help compare the overall economic output produced within a country?
Why should GDP per capita be interpreted cautiously as a measure of development?
choices: It is an average and does not show how income is distributed or every dimension of well-being
It measures only a country's total land area
It directly counts every person's wealth

questions.question: An agricultural region shifts from small farms to mechanized commercial production. What may happen to employment patterns?
choices: Fewer workers may be needed per unit of output, while other jobs may grow in processing or services

questions.question: A company chooses to locate near a university, skilled workers, and research facilities. Which factor is likely influencing its decision?
choices: Access to specialized knowledge and labor

questions.question: Why can a region's physical geography influence its economic activities?
choices: Physical geography fully determines every person's occupation
Resources have no effect on production
Climate, terrain, water, and resources can affect costs and opportunities

A coastal region has growing tourism but also faces seasonal employment and pressure on water resources. What is the best geographic analysis?
choices: Count visitor arrivals and ignore local effects
Consider economic benefits alongside seasonal labor and environmental limits
Assume tourism has identical impacts in every place
Treat water supply as unrelated to tourism

questions.question: What is one potential effect of a new highway linking an inland city to a seaport?
choices: It guarantees every local firm will expand
It eliminates trade with other regions
It may lower transport costs and change where firms choose to locate
It changes a region's natural resources

questions.question: A region's economy relies heavily on one crop. Why can this increase economic vulnerability?
choices: Crop specialization prevents all market changes
One crop guarantees stable household incomes
A single crop removes the need for trade
A disease, price drop, or weather shock can affect many producers at once

choices: Only the distance to the national capital
Jobs and incomes alongside environmental and health costs and who experiences them

questions.question: Why can access to reliable electricity affect a region's ability to attract industry?
choices: It determines the number of political parties
It removes the need for trained workers
It prevents goods from being transported
It supports production, communication, storage, and essential services

questions.question: A firm moves production to a place with lower wages but longer shipping routes and weaker infrastructure. What should it compare?
choices: Total costs and risks across labor, transport, reliability, and supply chains
